item.title: Ephemeral macOS Runners: A Fresh VM Per Job on Apple Silicon
item.description:
ephemerd gives every CI job a brand new environment and throws it away after. On Linux and Windows that environment is a container. On macOS it can’t be. Apple’s license wants macOS running on Apple hardware, so the Mac in my rack is the real thing. The isolation comes from a VM instead.

Each macOS job gets a fresh Virtualization.framework VM cloned from a base image. The job runs inside it. The VM is destroyed when the job finishes. That’s the same contract as the container path. Getting there took four fixes that I only found by running the fleet. This post walks the VM lifecycle and the three ways it bit me:

item.title: Kata Containers for CI: Boot Cost Isn't the Problem, File I/O Is
item.description: Of the three platforms ephemerd runs jobs on, Linux has the weakest isolation. Windows jobs get a Hyper-V isolated container with its own kernel. macOS jobs get a whole VM. A Linux job is an ordinary runc container sharing the host kernel. A kernel escape from a Linux job is a host compromise. Kata Containers fixes that by putting each container in a lightweight VM with its own kernel. It plugs into containerd as just another runtime handler. So I added it in #155, measured it, and left it off by default. This post is why.
